title: A fix round's start writes the group once, after auto_fixer is spawned with --round
objective: Starting a fix round writes the group record in one pool write after auto_fixer has been spawned, and auto_fixer takes its round from `--round` instead of reading it from the group.
outline: devloop/ticket_controller.py `start_fixer()` (line ~536) and `_start_job()` (line ~547): build argv with `--round`, `str(rnd)`; spawn first; then one `self.pool.update` that applies state `fixing`, `fix_round`, `fix_report`, the drops (`fix_retry`, `paused`), the `job`, the event `fix round <rnd>` then the event `fixer started`, and `close_pages(tx, gid, "superseded")` - for example let `_start_job` take an optional first event, state, drop and fields that it writes in its existing `set_group` call, or give `set_group` a way to write one extra event before `why`. devloop/auto_fixer.py: `main()` adds `ap.add_argument("--round", type=int)` and uses it for the inflight record; `fix(cfg, pool, gid, report, live=None, rnd=None)` uses `rnd` when given, else `int(group.get("fix_round") or 0)`. Update auto_fixer's docstring usage line. Why `--round`: with the write after the spawn, auto_fixer can read the group before the controller's write lands and would see the previous round. Measured on HEAD 4797416 with `osx.spawn` mocked: two pool commits, argv `--group g1 --report /r.json`, last two events `fix round 1`, `fixer started`; a failed spawn leaves the group `fixing`, `fix_round` 1, no job; `auto_fixer.py ... --round 2` exits 2 with `unrecognized arguments`. Out of scope: a controller that stops between the spawn and the write (the fixer then runs with no job recorded; the same window exists today between the spawn and the job write).
test_plan: Verifier writes cases for C1, C2 and C3; the implementer covers C4 and C5 (they hold today) and changes the old case of C5 in place if needed. Expect one more pool commit; `argv[-6:] == ["--group", "g1", "--report", "/r.json", "--round", "1"]` and `argv[1]` ends with `auto_fixer.py`; group state `fixing`, fix_round 1, fix_report `/r.json`, no fix_retry, no paused, job kind `fixer`, job out `/r.json`, job stamp pid 4242; the last two history events are `fix round 1`, `fixer started`. (The loop harness sets no min_free_memory_gib, so memory is never short.) C2: the same group without paused; the spawn side effect raises `osx.OSFailure("cannot start auto_fixer.py")`; `assertRaises(osx.OSFailure)`; pool commit count unchanged; group state `pr`, fix_round 0, fix_retry True, no job. C3: the fixture T69Acceptance.setUp builds (`self.config(max_rounds=1)`, `self.add(1)`, plan worker `{"1": ["red"]}` fixer `{"g1": ["nothing"]}`, `self.controller()`; measured: g1 then has fix_round 1 and only `runs/fix/g1/r1`); write a red report as T69Acceptance does; `self.plan(worker={"1": ["red"]}, fixer={"g1": ["nothing", "fix"]})` (the fake counts calls, so the next one is `fix`); run `self.run_py("auto_fixer.py", "--group", "g1", "--report", report, "--round", "2")`. Expect rc 0; the group's `fix_agent_round` == 2; its history holds `fixer agent started (round 2)`; the dir `os.path.join(self.tmp, "wt", "runs", "fix", "g1", "r2")` exists. Red today: rc 2 (measured). Each case takes a few seconds at most.

acceptance: C1 `Controller.start_fixer(gid, report, rnd)`, when memory is not short, spawns auto_fixer with an argv whose items after `<LOOP>/auto_fixer.py` are exactly `--group <gid> --report <report> --round <rnd>`, then makes exactly one pool commit, after which the group has state `fixing`, `fix_round` = rnd, `fix_report` = report, no `fix_retry`, no `paused`, `job` = {"kind": "fixer", "stamp": {pid of the spawned process, host, boot, started}, "out": report}, its pages acked `superseded` (as today), and history ending with the two events `fix round <rnd>` then `fixer started` (today's texts and order). Today: two commits and no `--round` (measured).

C2 When the spawn raises `osx.OSFailure`, `start_fixer` makes no pool commit, the group record is unchanged (state, fix_round, fix_retry and job stay as they were), and the OSFailure propagates as today. Today the group is left `fixing` with `fix_round` = rnd and no job (measured).

C3 `auto_fixer.py` accepts `--round N` (an int, optional). Given, N is the round it uses everywhere it reads the group's `fix_round` today: the run dir `runs/fix/<gid>/r<N>`, `mark_agent_round` (`fix_agent_round` = N, event `fixer agent started (round N)`), the inflight record's `round`, and the round passed on to `bring_back`, `_record_cases`, `_record_tests` and `memory.collect`. Without `--round` it reads the group's `fix_round` as today (existing tests start it without the flag). Today `--round` is refused with rc 2, `unrecognized arguments` (measured).

C4 Unchanged: the memory-short branch of start_fixer (one write: state `pr`, `fix_retry`, `fix_report`, `fix_round` = rnd - 1, no spawn); `start_regression` (if `_start_job` gains parameters they default to today's behaviour); exactly one `fixer started` event per fix round (test_regression_fixer.py line ~357).

C5 Old case changed in place if the implementation stops calling `_start_job(gid, kind, argv, out)` with those four arguments: `FixAgentRoundUnits.test_start_fixer_stores_the_report_and_drops_retry_and_pause` (tests_devloop/test_regression_fixer.py) replaces its 4-argument `_start_job` lambda with a patch of `ticket_controller.osx.spawn` returning `mock.Mock(pid=...)` and keeps its assertions (state `fixing`, `fix_round` 1, `fix_report` `/r.json`, no `fix_retry`, no `paused`) plus `job.kind == "fixer"`. test_pages.py `test_regression_and_fixer_start_ack_the_groups_pages`, test_machine.py `test_fix_round_due_while_short_waits_as_fix_retry` and the memory-short case that calls `start_fixer("g1", report, 1)` near test_machine.py line 1184 pass unchanged.

request:
Phase one, group 4 of the improvement plan: honest acceptance and reliability (D-100, D-102). Source: external audit
P0-2, P0-3, P0-6, P1-6, each confirmed by the main session reading the code; T main session agreed (2026-11-26).
Keep these as one group, three tickets.

4.1 Acceptance results must be honest.
- Problem (read in code): a skipped acceptance case (rc 0) counts as green; `red_check()` treats skip as red but
  expectedFailure is recorded as `pass`; nothing checks whether the worker edited the `T<N>Acceptance` cases.
- Layer 1: `run_cases()` requires each case to be exactly `pass`; `red_check()` requires exactly `fail`.
  expectedFailure is recorded as `xfail` (not pass).
- Layer 2: from round 2 on, a worker change that alters the `T<N>Acceptance` definitions is sent back. Compare by
  AST (classes and functions), and check the count of same-named definitions. A round that went through `--revise`
  (the ticket was rewritten) is not a violation. The verifier prompt gets one line: helpers specific to this ticket
  go inside the class.

4.2 Controller lock uses flock.
- Problem (read in code): `PidLock` creates an empty file and then writes JSON; two `actl run` starting at once can
  both take the lock.
- Do: keep the lock file (do not delete it), use `fcntl.flock`, clear the stamp on release; `controller_alive()` and
  existing tests keep passing.

4.3 start_fixer writes once.
- Do: `start_fixer()` writes the pool once, after the spawn, and passes `--round` to `auto_fixer.py`.

vision: an acceptance result means what it says, and two controllers cannot both run.
removes: the two-write path in start_fixer; the create-then-write PidLock path.
